question: A man's salary was increased by 10% to ₹55,000. What was his original salary?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

10% increase ⇒ 110% of original salary = ₹55,000

1% of original salary = 55,000 ÷ 110 = 500

100% (Original Salary) = 500 × 100 = ₹50,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increased Salary = ₹55,000

Percentage Increase = 10%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d99ad27b8e73a03c7eb132087175a19204ec5df10475e5f9d0939f7eef833d8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Original Salary = Increased Salary ÷ (1 + Increase%/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the original salary be x.

⇒ x + (10/100) × x = 55,000

⇒ x × (1 + 0.1) = 55,000

⇒ 1.1x = 55,000

⇒ x = 55,000 ÷ 1.1

⇒ x = 550,000 ÷ 11

⇒ x = 50,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase and Decrease

To increase a value by r%, multiply it by (100 + r)/100. To decrease a value by r%, multiply it by (100 − r)/100.

Fractional Equivalents

Using fractions can speed up calculations: 10% = 1/10. An increase of 1/10 means the new value is 11/10 of the original.

Base Change Rule

If A is r% more than B, then B is [r ÷ (100 + r)] × 100% less than A.
